name: Maths for Finance
title: Quant Apprentice
blurb: Calculus, matrices, statistics and random walks are the language underneath swap pricing, VaR and regression-based business analysis, so steady practice here makes the derivatives and strategy work far easier for Arin.

chapters.title: Algebra, functions, logs and exponentials
chapters.read: The first chapters of a 'maths for economics/business' textbook: solving equations, functions and their graphs, composition and inverses, exponent rules, and natural logs with applications to compound growth.
chapters.produce: Solve a 20-problem set (equations, composite functions, log rules) by hand, then build a spreadsheet showing ¥1,000,000 growing at 4% under annual versus continuous compounding for 30 years.

quiz.q: Money grows continuously at 5% a year: A = A0·e^(0.05t). How many years does it take to double? (2 decimals)
Evaluate log₂(64) − log₃(27).
quiz.ex: log₂ 64 = 6 and log₃ 27 = 3, so 6 − 3 = 3.

quiz.q: f(x) = 2x + 3 and g(x) = x². What is f(g(3))?
¥1,000,000 is invested at 4% compounded annually. What is it worth after 10 years? (nearest yen)
Which identity is correct for positive a and b?
opts: ln(a + b) = ln a × ln b
quiz.ex: Logs turn multiplication into addition; the other forms are common mistakes.

quiz.q: What is the domain of f(x) = ln x (real numbers)?
quiz.ex: The natural log is defined only for strictly positive inputs; ln 0 is undefined.

chapters.title: Differential calculus
chapters.read: The differentiation chapters of a maths-for-economics textbook: limits and slopes, power, product, quotient and chain rules, derivatives of e^x and ln x, and finding maxima and minima with first and second derivatives.
chapters.produce: Work 25 differentiation exercises by hand and solve two optimisation problems (profit maximisation and minimum average cost), checking each answer numerically in a spreadsheet.

quiz.q: f(x) = 3x⁴ − 2x. What is f′(1)?
f(x) = e^(2x). What is f′(0)?
quiz.ex: By the chain rule f′(x) = 2e^(2x), so f′(0) = 2.

quiz.q: f(x) = x² − 6x + 10. What is the minimum value of f?
f(x) = x·ln x. What is f′(e)?
quiz.ex: Product rule: f′(x) = ln x + 1, so f′(e) = 1 + 1 = 2.

quiz.q: At a point where f′(x) = 0 and f″(x) > 0, the function has…
quiz.ex: Positive second derivative means the curve bends upward, so a flat point is a valley.

quiz.q: What is the derivative of (3x + 1)⁵?
quiz.ex: Chain rule: 5(3x + 1)⁴ times the inner derivative 3.

chapters.title: Integral calculus
chapters.read: The integration chapters of a maths-for-economics textbook: antiderivatives, definite integrals as areas, the fundamental theorem of calculus, integrating e^x and 1/x, and applications such as present value of a continuous cash-flow stream.
chapters.produce: Work 20 integration exercises by hand and compute the present value of a continuous income stream both exactly and with a 12-step numerical approximation in a spreadsheet.

quiz.q: Evaluate ∫ from 0 to 2 of 3x² dx.
quiz.ex: Antiderivative x³; 2³ − 0 = 8.

quiz.q: Evaluate ∫ from 0 to 1 of eˣ dx. (3 decimals)
What is the area under f(x) = 2x + 1 between x = 1 and x = 3?
quiz.ex: Antiderivative x² + x: (9 + 3) − (1 + 1) = 10.

quiz.q: A stream pays ¥100 per year continuously for 5 years. Discounting continuously at 5%, what is its present value? (2 decimals)
What is an antiderivative of 1/x (x ≠ 0)?
quiz.ex: The derivative of ln|x| is 1/x; the power rule fails for exponent −1.

quiz.q: By the fundamental theorem of calculus, d/dx of ∫ from a to x of f(t) dt equals…
opts: the area under f from a to x
quiz.ex: Differentiation undoes integration with respect to the upper limit.

chapters.title: Linear algebra: vectors, matrices and systems
chapters.read: The matrix algebra chapters of a maths-for-economics textbook or a free linear algebra lecture series: vectors and dot products, matrix multiplication, determinants and inverses, solving linear systems, and portfolio variance as wᵀΣw.
chapters.produce: Solve five 3×3 systems by elimination and by matrix inverse (spreadsheet MINVERSE/MMULT), and compute the variance of a 3-asset portfolio from a covariance matrix.

quiz.q: What is the dot product of (1, 2, 3) and (4, −1, 2)?
What is the determinant of the matrix [[3, 2], [1, 4]]?
Solve 2x + y = 7 and x − y = 2. What is x?
quiz.ex: Adding the equations: 3x = 9, so x = 3 (and y = 1).

quiz.q: Two assets with weights 0.5 and 0.5, variances 0.04 and 0.09, covariance 0.012. What is the portfolio variance wᵀΣw? (4 decimals)
A square matrix has an inverse exactly when…
quiz.ex: A zero determinant means the rows are linearly dependent, so no inverse exists.

quiz.q: A is 2×3 and B is 3×4. What is the size of AB?
quiz.ex: Inner dimensions (3 and 3) match; the result takes the outer dimensions 2×4.

chapters.title: Probability basics and distributions
chapters.read: The probability chapters of an introductory statistics textbook: events and rules, conditional probability and Bayes, random variables, expectation and variance, and the binomial, Poisson and normal distributions.
chapters.produce: Simulate 10,000 rolls of two dice and 10,000 binomial draws in a spreadsheet or Python and compare the simulated frequencies and means with the theoretical values.

quiz.q: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability their sum is 7? (decimal, 4 places)
quiz.ex: 6 of the 36 equally likely outcomes give 7: 6/36 = 0.1667.

quiz.q: X takes values 0, 10, 20 with probabilities 0.5, 0.3, 0.2. What is Var(X)?
A fair coin is tossed 4 times. What is the probability of exactly 2 heads? (decimal)
X ~ Normal(mean 100, standard deviation 15). What is P(X < 130)? (3 decimals)
Events A and B are independent. Which statement holds?
quiz.ex: Independence means knowing B does not change A's probability, so the joint probability is the product.

quiz.q: Which distribution is the natural model for the number of trade fails arriving in a day at a constant average rate?
quiz.ex: The Poisson distribution counts independent events occurring at a constant average rate in a fixed interval.

chapters.title: Statistics: estimation, confidence intervals and tests
chapters.read: The inference chapters of an introductory statistics textbook: sample mean and standard deviation, sampling distributions and the central limit theorem, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing with z and t statistics, p-values and error types.
chapters.produce: Take a real public dataset (e.g. daily returns of a stock index you download yourself), estimate mean and volatility, build a 95% confidence interval for the mean, and test whether the mean return is zero.

quiz.q: What is the sample mean of 4, 8, 6, 10, 7?
What is the sample standard deviation (divide by n − 1) of 4, 8, 6, 10, 7? (3 decimals)
quiz.ex: Squared deviations from 7: 9, 1, 1, 9, 0 = 20. 20/4 = 5, √5 ≈ 2.236.

quiz.q: Sample of n = 100, mean 50, standard deviation 10. Using z = 1.96, what is the upper bound of the 95% confidence interval for the mean?
H₀: μ = 100. A sample of 36 has mean 103; the population standard deviation is 12. What is the z statistic?
What does a p-value of 0.03 mean?
opts: The null hypothesis has a 3% chance of being true
The alternative hypothesis has a 97% chance of being true
If the null hypothesis were true, a result at least this extreme would occur about 3% of the time
quiz.ex: A p-value is computed assuming H₀; it is not the probability that H₀ is true.

quiz.q: What is a Type I error?
opts: Failing to reject a false null hypothesis
Rejecting the null hypothesis when it is actually true
quiz.ex: Type I is a false positive; Type II is failing to reject a false null.

chapters.title: Regression and intro econometrics
chapters.read: The simple and multiple regression chapters of an introductory econometrics textbook: OLS estimates, interpretation of coefficients, R², standard errors and t-tests, and common problems (omitted variables, multicollinearity, heteroskedasticity).
chapters.produce: Estimate a stock's beta by regressing its daily returns on an index's returns in a spreadsheet (SLOPE/LINEST or Python), report the coefficient, its t-statistic and R², and write three sentences interpreting them.

quiz.q: Data: x = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and y = 2, 4, 5, 4, 5. What is the OLS slope of y on x?
Same data (slope 0.6, x̄ = 3, ȳ = 4). What is the OLS intercept?
quiz.ex: Intercept = ȳ − slope × x̄ = 4 − 1.8 = 2.2.

quiz.q: Same data: total sum of squares is 6 and the fitted line is ŷ = 2.2 + 0.6x. What is R²?
Using ŷ = 2.2 + 0.6x, what is the predicted y at x = 6?
In a regression, what does heteroskedasticity mean?
opts: The variance of the error term changes across observations
Two explanatory variables are highly correlated
The errors have a non-zero mean
The relationship between y and x is non-linear
quiz.ex: Heteroskedasticity is non-constant error variance; high correlation between regressors is multicollinearity.

quiz.q: A coefficient estimate is 0.8 with standard error 0.2. Roughly what does its t-statistic tell you?
opts: t = 0.16, so the coefficient is insignificant
t = 4, so the coefficient is clearly significantly different from zero at usual levels
t = 1, so the result is borderline
t cannot be computed without R²
quiz.ex: t = estimate / standard error = 0.8/0.2 = 4, well above about 2.

chapters.title: Intro to stochastic processes and random walks
chapters.read: An introductory chapter on stochastic processes for finance: random walks, the Markov property, Brownian motion and its independent normal increments, geometric Brownian motion for stock prices, and a first look at Itô's lemma.
chapters.produce: Simulate 1,000 paths of a symmetric random walk and of geometric Brownian motion in Python or a spreadsheet, plot 20 paths, and check that the simulated mean and variance at the end match the theory.

quiz.q: A symmetric random walk moves +1 or −1 with equal probability each step. What is the standard deviation of its position after 100 steps (starting at 0)?
quiz.ex: Each step has variance 1; 100 independent steps give variance 100, so SD = 10.

quiz.q: W is a standard Brownian motion. What is Var(W₄ − W₁)?
quiz.ex: Increments are normal with variance equal to elapsed time: 4 − 1 = 3.

quiz.q: A stock follows geometric Brownian motion with drift μ = 8% per year and S₀ = 100. What is E[S₁] (after 1 year)? (2 decimals)
A walk steps +1 with probability 0.6 and −1 with probability 0.4. What is its expected position after 50 steps (starting at 0)?
What is the Markov property?
opts: The process always returns to its starting value
All increments have the same sign
The future evolution depends only on the current state, not on the path taken to get there
quiz.ex: A Markov process has no memory beyond its present value.

quiz.q: Which statement about standard Brownian motion increments is correct?
opts: Increments are uniformly distributed between −1 and 1
Increments over consecutive periods are perfectly correlated
Increment variance equals the square of the time elapsed
Non-overlapping increments are independent and normally distributed with mean 0 and variance equal to the time elapsed
quiz.ex: W_t − W_s ~ N(0, t − s), independent of the past.

boss.q: Profit P(q) = −2q² + 40q − 50. What is the maximum profit?
Evaluate ∫ from 1 to 4 of √x dx. (3 decimals)
Solve x + y + z = 6, 2x − y + z = 3, x + 2y − z = 2. What is z?
boss.ex: Adding eq2+eq3: 3x + y = 5; eq1+eq3: 2x + 3y = 8. So x = 1, y = 2, then z = 6 − 3 = 3.

boss.q: What continuously compounded rate is equivalent to 5% compounded annually, in %? (3 decimals)
A condition affects 1% of people. A test detects it 90% of the time and gives a false positive 5% of the time. Given a positive test, what is the probability of having the condition? (3 decimals)
Sample n = 400, mean 2.5, standard deviation 4. Using z = 1.96, what is the LOWER bound of the 95% confidence interval for the mean?
X ~ Poisson(λ = 3). What is P(X = 2)? (3 decimals)
A stock follows GBM with μ = 10% and σ = 20% per year. What is the expected value of the 1-year log return ln(S₁/S₀), in %?
Which property must every valid covariance matrix have?
opts: It is symmetric and positive semi-definite
boss.ex: Cov(X,Y) = Cov(Y,X) gives symmetry, and any portfolio variance wᵀΣw must be ≥ 0. Negative covariances and zero determinants are allowed.

boss.q: Which of these processes is a martingale?
opts: A stock price under GBM with positive drift μ
A deterministic series growing 1% per step
boss.ex: A martingale's expected next value equals its current value; any positive drift breaks this.
